BLOCKER: `edpsvc/memoryHandle` derives the ACL principal from the client-supplied `?user=` query param; any caller can set `user=alice` and read other users' `private` entries. The principal must come from the authenticated session (JWT/identity), not the request.
The same handler lets the client set `Owner` on POST, enabling spoofed ownership and planting entries into another user's private view; ownership must be derived server-side.
MAJOR: Backward-compat break: previously `scope.Source` was compared against `acl_scope` in SQL; it now filters the new `source` column. Existing clients passing `?source=private`/`project` will silently get zero results instead of ACL-scoped results.
AC requires the kinds filter parameter named `kinds`; the handler exposes `types` instead — acceptance mismatch, and a second param name will be needed later.

`Put`'s `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE` has no tenant/owner match guard; combined with client-settable `TenantID`/`Owner`, any in-tenant principal can overwrite any memory row (including `policy`/`failure` kinds) if RLS is absent or permissive.

`vectorAvailable` uses `sync.Once` and swallows query errors, permanently caching "no vector" for the lifetime of a long-lived `MemoryStore` after one transient failure; cache the positive case, re-probe or bound the negative result.

Migration swallows `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS` for extension creation and HNSW index build with no log/metric, so pgvector silently degrades with zero observability; downstream teams cannot tell FTS-only mode from a bug.

Integration tests `t.Skip` when `PF_DB_DSN` is unset — the ACL-leakage and ranking guarantees are only verified when someone remembers to set the DSN; CI wiring/required-tag is not evident in the diff.
MINOR: `websearch_to_tsquery('english', ...)` hardcodes English; the tsv column does the same — no per-locale path for multi-language tenants.
Hybrid ranking weights (0.7/0.3) are magic numbers inline; extract as named, documented constants (and note the FTS and cosine scores are not calibrated to the same scale, so ranking is heuristic).
POST accepts unbounded `Content`/`Embedding` payload sizes (only dim is validated) — add a max-size guard consistent with other endpoints.

Down migration intentionally keeps `content/source/owner/embedding` but drops `tsv`; a down→up round trip silently loses the derived index state for large tables (rebuild cost) — worth a comment or lock_timeout note.
`Search` with a supplied vector but zero rows carrying embeddings returns nothing rather than degrading to FTS-only; consider falling back explicitly.
No metrics/logging distinguishing FTS-only vs hybrid execution; add an observable signal for the chosen path.
NIT: `formatVector` reimplements pgvector serialization; when pgvector is actually available, prefer the official driver codec (or assert round-trip equality in a test) to avoid subtle precision/NaN divergences.
`MemoryEntry.Score` is exported in API responses with no doc that it is internal ranking state — consider omitting or namespacing it in the JSON payload.
Test cleanup deletes tenants but relies on cascade for `memory` rows; make the FK/cascade assumption explicit.
